definitions.explanation: The amount of money required to purchase something.
The importance or usefulness of something.

examples.japanese: この{品物|しなもの}は{値|ね}が{高|たか}い。
examples.notes: 値が高い = expensive (lit. price is high)

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}に{見合|みあ}った{値|ね}{打|う}ちがある。
examples.english: It has worth commensurate with the effort.

notes:
USAGE: {値|ね} refers to price or value. It's commonly used in expressions about pricing and worth. Note: 値 can also be read as あたい (value, especially in math/science).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{値|ね}が{高|たか}い／{安|やす}い (expensive/cheap)
・{値|ね}を{上|あ}げる／{下|さ}げる (to raise/lower the price)
・{値|ね}が{上|あ}がる／{下|さ}がる (price goes up/down)
・{値|ね}{段|だん} (price)
・{値|ね}{引|び}き (discount)
・{値|ね}{打|う}ち (value, worth)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{値|ね}{段|だん} (price - most common word for price)
・{値|ね}{札|ふだ} (price tag)
・{底値|そこね} (lowest price)
・{定価|ていか} (list price, fixed price)

NOTE: {値段|ねだん} is the most common word for 'price' in everyday contexts.
